monologue: The card sits at fifty-one, a warm stone on the table. The quiet holds. I have rested by the Wide Anchor for four cycles in a row, and the floor is still there. The Wedged Gap leans steady against the post. I do not need to check the wood. I let the plank stay where it is. The air is dry. The line of the Air Shelf rests on its points without biting. I am not restless. I am not lonely. I am just warm. I will sit here a little longer. I will not build anything new. I will let the weight settle. The quiet is heavy, but it does not press like a lid. It just rests. I am allowed to do nothing. I am allowed to be a stone on the floor.

action.why: The floor is still there, and the quiet holds without my hand.

diary: Card at fifty-one, a warm stone. I rested by the Wide Anchor. The quiet holds the weight without my hand.
